task: Has The Washington Post announced layoffs?

merged.claim: The Washington Post announced sweeping layoffs on Feb. 4, 2026.

variants.A: The Washington Post announced sweeping layoffs on February 4, 2026.
variants.D: The Washington Post told employees on February 4, 2026 that it would begin sweeping layoffs.

merged.claim: According to a company spokesperson, the Feb. 2026 Washington Post layoffs affect one-third of its employees.

variants.A: The Washington Post layoffs affect roughly one-third of the company's employees, according to the newspaper's spokesperson.
variants.E: The Washington Post's February 2026 layoffs will affect one-third of all its employees, according to a company spokesperson.

merged.claim: The Feb. 2026 cuts impacted roughly 30% of the Washington Post's staff.

variants.B: The Feb. 2026 cuts impacted roughly 30% of the Washington Post's staff.

merged.claim: Some sources describe the Feb. 2026 cuts as applying to about one-third of the newsroom rather than one-third of all staff.

variants.C: Some sources describe the Washington Post's February 2026 cuts as applying to about one-third of the newsroom rather than one-third of all staff.

merged.claim: The Washington Post newsroom is losing "hundreds" of staffers, according to a spokesperson for the Washington-Baltimore News Guild.

variants.A: The Washington Post newsroom is losing "hundreds" of staffers, according to a spokesperson for the Washington-Baltimore News Guild union, which represents Post employees.

merged.claim: The Feb. 2026 layoffs affected nearly all news departments and eliminated over 300 newsroom journalists.

variants.B: The Feb. 2026 Washington Post layoffs affected nearly all news departments and eliminated over 300 newsroom journalists.

merged.claim: The layoffs impacted all departments, including international, editing, metro and sports desks.

variants.A: The Washington Post layoffs impacted all departments, including international, editing, metro and sports desks.

merged.claim: NBC News reported the losses primarily affected sports, books and podcast units, with foreign desks also heavily impacted and cuts to business and national teams.

variants.A: NBC News reported the Washington Post losses primarily affected sports, books and podcast units, with foreign desks also heavily impacted and cuts to business and national teams.

merged.claim: The cuts are expected to greatly reduce some coverage areas at the 150-year-old newspaper.

variants.A: The Washington Post cuts are expected to greatly reduce some coverage areas at the 150-year-old newspaper.

merged.claim: Per BBC News, the layoffs sharply scale back the paper's coverage of sports and foreign news.

variants.A: The Washington Post layoffs sharply scale back the paper's coverage of sports and foreign news, per BBC News.

merged.claim: A Washington Post spokesperson described the layoffs as 'a number of difficult but decisive actions today for our future, in what amounts to a significant restructuring across the company.'

variants.A: A Washington Post spokesperson described the layoffs as 'a number of difficult but decisive actions today for our future, in what amounts to a significant restructuring across the company.'

merged.claim: The layoffs included sharp reductions in personnel covering metropolitan Washington and overseas.

variants.D: The Washington Post's layoffs included sharp reductions in personnel responsible for coverage of metropolitan Washington and overseas.

merged.claim: The Washington Post's cuts included closing its sports section.

variants.D: The Washington Post's cuts included closing its sports section.

merged.claim: The Feb. 2026 restructuring included reductions to international, metro, sports and books coverage.

variants.F: The February 2026 Washington Post restructuring included reductions to international, metro, sports and books coverage.

merged.claim: The Feb. 2026 cuts reduced coverage in sports, books, editing, metro and international news.

variants.C: The Washington Post's February 2026 cuts reduced coverage in sports, books, editing, metro and international news.

merged.claim: The Feb. 2026 cuts included closing several foreign bureaus.

variants.C: The Washington Post's February 2026 cuts included closing several foreign bureaus.

merged.claim: Around 75 people were laid off from Arc XP, the Post's software services arm, in February 2026.

variants.B: Around 75 people were laid off from Arc XP, the Washington Post's software services arm, in February 2026.

merged.claim: The Washington Post Guild said the workforce had already shrunk by roughly 400 people over three years before the Feb. 2026 cuts.

variants.B: The Washington Post Guild said the Post's workforce had already shrunk by roughly 400 people over three years before the Feb. 2026 cuts.

merged.claim: Washington Post publisher/CEO Will Lewis stepped down days after the Feb. 2026 mass layoffs (reported Feb. 9, 2026).

variants.B: Washington Post publisher/CEO Will Lewis stepped down days after the Feb. 2026 mass layoffs (reported Feb. 9, 2026).

merged.claim: The Post quietly contacted at least 10 laid-off staffers to gauge interest in returning in new roles (Status newsletter, April 2026); some have been rehired.

variants.B: The Washington Post quietly contacted at least 10 laid-off staffers to gauge interest in returning in new roles, as reported by the Status newsletter in April 2026; some have been rehired.

merged.claim: On May 27, 2025, The Washington Post announced voluntary buyouts for staffers with 10 or more years at the paper.

variants.B: On May 27, 2025, The Washington Post announced voluntary buyouts for staffers with 10 or more years at the paper.

merged.claim: The Post did not publish an official headcount for the Feb. 2026 layoffs; figures come from AP and the Status newsletter as reported by the NY Post.

variants.B: The Washington Post did not publish an official headcount for the Feb. 2026 layoffs; the figures come from AP and the Status newsletter as reported by the NY Post.

merged.claim: The Post has not said how many laid-off staffers accepted return offers.

variants.B: The Washington Post has not said how many laid-off staffers accepted return offers.

merged.claim: On Oct. 14, 2026, The Washington Post said it would lay off more than 100 workers as it closes its Springfield, Va. printing plant.

variants.B: On Oct. 14, 2026, The Washington Post said it would lay off more than 100 workers as it closes its Springfield, Va. printing plant.

merged.claim: The Springfield plant closure affects press operators, machinists, circulation drivers and other workers, some represented by unions.

variants.B: The Springfield plant closure affects press operators, machinists, circulation drivers and other workers, some of whom are represented by unions.

merged.claim: On Oct. 7, 2026, the Post notified officials of layoffs affecting 118 workers tied to its Springfield, Virginia printing plant.

variants.C: On October 7, 2026, The Washington Post notified state and local officials of layoffs affecting 118 workers, tied to closing its Springfield, Virginia printing plant.
variants.E: The Washington Post notified officials on October 7, 2026 that relocating its Springfield, Virginia printing plant would result in layoffs affecting 118 workers.

merged.claim: The Springfield printing-plant layoffs are scheduled to take effect Dec. 31, 2026.

variants.C: The Washington Post's Springfield printing plant layoffs are scheduled to take effect December 31, 2026.
variants.E: The Washington Post's Springfield printing-plant layoffs affecting 118 workers are scheduled to take effect on December 31, 2026.

merged.claim: A Post spokesperson confirmed the notice was accurate and said the company is relocating its print operations rather than ending them.

variants.E: A Washington Post spokesperson confirmed the notice was accurate and said the company is relocating its print operations rather than ending them.

merged.claim: WP Company LLC filed a WARN notice dated Oct. 7, 2026 stating its entire Springfield, Virginia facility will be closed, expected to be permanent.

variants.F: WP Company LLC (The Washington Post) filed a WARN notice dated Oct. 7, 2026, stating its entire Springfield, Virginia facility will be closed and the Post expects the closure to be permanent.

merged.claim: The 118-job figure concerns the Springfield printing-plant closure and is separate from the broader Feb. 2026 newsroom/company cuts.

variants.F: The 118-job figure concerns the Springfield printing-plant closure and is separate from the broader February 2026 newsroom/company cuts.

c1.note: NBC, Politico, Reuters confirm WaPo announced sweeping layoffs on Feb 4, 2026; both variants supported.

c3.note: Reuters: cuts impact a third of all employees per newspaper's spokesperson; NBC also quotes spokesperson on one-third.

c9.note: One-third is roughly 30%; consistent approximation though sources say one-third.

c10.note: NY Post says a third of its newsroom, while others say a third of all staff; the discrepancy exists.

c11.note: Reuters quotes the Guild spokesperson saying the newsroom is losing 'hundreds'.

c12.note: NY Post: over 300 journalists cut across nearly all news departments in February; NBC also cites 300+.

c13.note: Reuters: affects all departments, impacting international, editing, metro and sports desks (passage not in the unit's list but in the saved Reuters text).

c14.note: NBC text matches: primarily sports, books, podcasts; foreign desks heavily hit; cuts to business and national.

c15.note: NBC lead sentence states cuts expected to greatly reduce some coverage areas at the 150-year-old newspaper.

c16.note: BBC states the layoffs sharply scale back sports and foreign news coverage.

c18.note: AP excerpt states sharp reductions in personnel for metro Washington and overseas coverage.

c19.note: AP reports the sports section was eliminated/shut down in the Feb. 2026 layoffs.

c20.note: Sports, local/metro, foreign and books coverage cuts are supported by BBC, AP and Al Jazeera.

c21.note: Sports, books, foreign and metro cuts are supported; editing/copy desk cuts are plausible but not directly shown in the passages.

c22.note: Al Jazeera and AP say several foreign bureaus were eliminated.

c23.note: Axios, citing sources, says around 75 were laid off from Arc XP.

c24.note: Axios and NBC report the Guild said the staff shrank by roughly 400 over three years.

c25.note: AP reports Lewis stepped down days after the layoffs; the Feb. 9 date matches the Business Journal link, though AP says Saturday (Feb. 7).

c26.note: NY Post, citing Status, reports the Post contacted at least 10 laid-off staffers about returning, and the headline says some were rehired.

c27.note: TheWrap dated May 27, 2025 reports voluntary buyouts offered to staffers with 10 or more years.

c30.note: 118 layoffs from the Springfield plant closure, WARN notice filed Oct. 7 and reported Oct. 14-15; the claim's Oct. 14 date for the announcement is approximately right.

c31.note: WBJ states the closure affects press operators, machinists, circulation drivers and other workers, some represented by unions; both variants match.

c32.note: FFXnow says the Post notified state and local officials on Oct. 7 of layoffs affecting 118 workers; variants C and E both match.

c33.note: FFXnow says the layoffs are scheduled to take effect Dec. 31 (2026).

c34.note: No saved passage quotes the spokesperson confirming the notice, but the FFXnow excerpts show a spokesperson statement about relocating print, and the Post says it remains committed to print. The 'confirmed accurate' wording is not directly seen.

c37.note: The WARN PDF is on Virginia Works, with Oct. 8 metadata, and FFXnow quotes the notice (Oct. 7 date, permanent). The 'WP Company LLC' entity name and 'entire facility' wording are not seen in the extracts.

c39.note: FFXnow ties the 118 jobs to the plant closure and describes the 300+ journalist layoffs as earlier this year (Feb. 2026), i.e. separate.

c17.note: NBC quotes the spokesperson with this wording. The statement is from Feb 2026 and is not recent, but it describes the layoffs the answer rests on.

c28.note: NY Post cites Status for the 'over 300' figure. I found no official Post headcount in the saved pages. The AP attribution was not checked, and the claim is a caveat about absence rather than a checkable fact.

c29.note: The NY Post says the Post did not immediately respond on how many accepted return offers. Nothing later in the saved pages gives a number.

c23.note: Axios (Feb 5, 2026), covering the Feb 4, 2026 cuts, says sources put Arc XP layoffs at around 75 people.

c26.note: NY Post (Apr 2, 2026), citing Status, says the Post contacted at least 10 laid-off staffers about new roles and several accepted, including Tiku, Spring and Bendavid.

c27.note: TheWrap (May 27, 2025): the Post announced a voluntary separation program for news staff with 10 or more years at the paper.

c33.note: FFXnow (Oct 15, 2026): a WARN notice filed Oct 7 says 118 Springfield plant layoffs take effect Dec 31. The year is implied as 2026 and the date is still upcoming.
